title: GM 2.4L (LAF/LEA): excessive oil consumption, pistons and rings
summary: GM bulletin 13-06-01-003J: test oil consumption, and if it exceeds 1 quart per 2,000 miles, replace the pistons and rings. 2010 Equinox and Terrain also got a 10-year/120,000-mile special coverage.

specs.name: Repair threshold
specs.value: More than 1 quart per 2,000 miles (0.946 L per 3,200 km)

specs.name: Repair
specs.value: Replace pistons and rings; no machining or honing of the bores

specs.name: Reads empty when
specs.value: About 1.25 qt (1.18 L) or more low: no oil shows on the stick

specs.name: Special coverage 14159D (2010 Equinox / Terrain, LAF)
specs.value: 10 years or 120,000 miles from in-service date; dealer replaces the 4 piston assemblies

steps.text: Verify the ECM has the latest calibration, which limits the oil life monitor to a maximum of 7,500 miles (GM Customer Satisfaction Bulletin 12312).
Inspect for oil leaks that would explain the loss and repair them first.
Run an oil consumption test per the latest version of GM bulletin 01-06-01-011. Do not overfill: let the level drop below the cross-hatched area before adding.
When measuring, the amount of oil needed to return to the starting mark is the amount consumed. Remember the notches are not equal (0.24 qt upper, 0.14 qt lower).
If consumption is over 1 quart per 2,000 miles, record the rate and replace the pistons and rings.
Uneven "zebra stripe" bore finish is acceptable with new pistons and rings. Engine replacement and bore machining are not needed. Do not modify the PCV system.
